person_note: The event quotes repeatedly expose Sallie as a participating I/we narrator, while the dialogue and generic-you aphorisms are local or gnomic rather than competing narrative strands. A sustained authorized opening agrees, and multiple whole-book descriptions—including Walls's own discussion of composing the novel in first-person present—identify Sallie as the narrator. No source indicates sustained sections in another person. The only limitation is that the Tier A prose evidence covers the opening rather than the entire novel, but the distributed quote evidence and independent whole-book descriptions resolve that scope limitation.
